History:
- 45-year-old female reports sudden onset (today) of right-sided pleuritic pain “catches in back when I breathe deeply,” associated with shortness of breath.
- Additional symptoms: low-grade subjective fever (not formally measured), hemoptysis on two occasions today, awareness of heartbeat, fatigue and reduced exercise tolerance for ~2 weeks.
- No preceding upper-respiratory illness described; felt “fine” until yesterday.
- Denies recent long-haul flights, prior venous thromboembolism, or family history of clots.
- Never smoker. Works at a desk job; lives alone in a flat with one cat.

Past Medical History:
- Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE).
- No other chronic illnesses reported.
- Medications: Methotrexate – dose/route/frequency not documented (last dose taken this morning).
- Allergies: No known drug or other allergies.
- No prior thrombosis, hospitalizations, or surgeries noted.

Physical Examination:
(Remote/limited video assessment)
- General: Alert, conversant, appears clinically stable.
- Pulse (patient-measured radial count): 11–12 beats/10 s ≈ 66–72 bpm, regular.
- Capillary refill: brisk.
- Oropharynx: normal visualization; no obvious throat swelling.
- Cervical lymph nodes: patient self-palpated; none appreciated.
- No gross respiratory distress observed on camera.

Impression:
Acute pleuritic chest pain with hemoptysis and low-grade fever — likely lower-respiratory tract infection/pneumonia; pulmonary embolism and other serious pathology (e.g., malignancy) need exclusion.

Management Plan:
- Arrange same-day face-to-face GP review for:
  • Chest auscultation.
  • Full vital signs (BP, temperature, respiratory rate, O2 saturation, repeat HR).
- Consider chest X-ray and/or further imaging if examination suggests consolidation, PE, or mass.
- Empiric oral antibiotic therapy to be started if bacterial pneumonia suspected once examined (no allergies reported).
- Provide support-team phone number for appointment scheduling today.
- Safety-net: seek urgent care/ED if worsening breathlessness, increased hemoptysis, high fever, dizziness, or chest pain escalation.

Patient Summary:
45-year-old woman with SLE on methotrexate presents with one-day history of right-sided pleuritic chest pain, mild fever, and scant hemoptysis. Remote exam stable; concern for pneumonia versus other intrathoracic pathology. Same-day in-person review and possible antibiotics planned.

Key Takeaways:
- Attend clinic today for chest examination and vitals.
- Call support team immediately to book appointment; go to ED if symptoms worsen.
- Likely infection rather than cancer, but follow-up imaging may be required if not improving.

Next Steps:
- Same-day GP appointment.
- Possible CXR, labs (CBC, CRP) depending on findings.
- Begin antibiotics if indicated.
- Re-assessment within 48–72 h or sooner if deterioration.
- Consider further work-up (e.g., CT chest, D-dimer) if PE or malignancy suspected.
